title: UNCCD COP17 Closes in Ulaanbaatar Without Binding Drought Protocol After African Group Walkout
detail: The 17th session of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD COP17), held August 17–28, 2026, in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, under the theme 'Restoring Land. Restoring Hope,' concluded on August 28 without agreement on a binding global drought protocol. The United States drew a 'red line' against any international drought instrument — binding or voluntary — arguing drought is fundamentally a domestic governance issue best handled through existing tools like the UNCCD Drought Toolbox and bilateral arrangements. The Africa Group, which has pushed for a legally binding protocol since the impasse at COP16 in Riyadh (December 2024), staged a coordinated walkout from negotiating rooms in protest, arguing that treating drought purely as a national matter undercuts existing Convention commitments and blocks access to climate finance. UNCCD Deputy Executive Secretary Andrea Meza Murillo said 'most of the parties are recognising that this is a global challenge,' underscoring that the US position does not reflect the mainstream view among parties. Negotiations on the drought framework were postponed roughly two years to COP18, to be hosted by Egypt. The conference did register other outcomes, including a zero-nominal-growth secretariat budget and the UN General Assembly's declaration of 2026 as the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists.
